senses.gloss:
पूयमान-यवम्, ind. at the time of winnowing
barley; [cf. पूत-यवम्.]

पूय् पूय्, cl. 1. P. A. पूयति, -ते, पुपूय,
-ये, पूयिष्यति, -ते, पूयितुम्, Ved. to
become foul or putrid, to putrefy, stink; to be dis-
solved; to split or cleave (?); [cf. Zend pū, ‘to
stink;’ pui-ti, ‘putridness:’ Gr. πύ-θ-ω, πΰθ-ο-μαι,
πυθ-ε-δών, Πυθ-ώ, Πύθων, πύ-ο-ν, πυέ-ω, πῦος:
Lat. pūs, pus-cīnu-s, pur-u-lentu-s, put-eo, puter,
put-i-du-s, pud-ere: Goth. ful-s, ‘foul:’ Old Norse
fūi, ‘putridness;’ fūk-i, ‘a stench:’ Angl. Sax.
fūl = Eng. foul = Mod. Germ. faul: Lith. pú-ti,
‘to putrefy;’ pú-d-au, ‘I cause to putrefy;’ pú-lei,
‘pus:’ Hib. putar, ‘putrid, stinking.’]

पूय, अस्, अम्, m. n. pus, purulent matter, sup-
puration, discharge from an ulcer or wound.
—पूय-
भुज्, क्, क्, क्, eating purulent carcasses.
—पूय-
रक्त, अस्, m., scil. रोग, ‘having purulent blood,’
a kind of disease of the nose with discharge of puru-
lent blood or sanies; (अम्), n. discharge of sanies
from the nostrils; ichor, sanies.
—पूय-वाह, अस्,
m. ‘filthy-streamed,’ N. of a hell (in which filthy
water flows).
—पूय-शोणित, अम्, n. purulent blood,
ichor, sanies.
—पूयारि (˚य-अरि˚), इस्, m. ‘hostile
to suppuration,’ the Nimb tree, Azadirachta Indica
(the leaves of which are used to produce dis-
persion or absorption of purulent matter).
—पूया-
लस (˚य-अल्˚), अस्, m. a particular disease of the
juncture of the eye; suppuration at the joints, white
swelling.
—पूयोद (˚य-उद), अस्, m. ‘having
stinking water,’ N. of a hell; [cf. पूय-वाह.]

पूयन, अम्, n. pus, discharge from a wound
or sore.
